answer: Each identity locks a 60 credit bond and files five quill-signed contributions in the beacon ledger before the horizon closes. Only distinct key-bound contributions count; anyone may recompute the count. Below five at the horizon the bond is forfeited. A fresh set costs 45 credits first, rising 3 per later identity as the beacon pool drains, so the 1000th set costs 3042 and 1000 sets cost 1543500. A rented portfolio fails: rented entries carry the lender quill key, which the ledger rejects, burning the bond. An honest identity files its own five, pays 45 once, and recovers its bond.
